messages:
Ana Varela: quick design thread  about adding persistent annotation pins to the version-history timeline. idea: let users pin notes (e.g., 'hotfix applied', 'rollout paused for rate limit') that remain attached to a version chip in the timeline. mock: https://img.redwood.dev/mock/timeline-annotation-pins.png

Tom - Eng: nice feature. two implementation caveats: 1) the timeline is virtualized for long histories, so pins must be stored server-side and we should render only when chip is in viewport. 2) pins should not change DOM order for screen readers; render pins as visually associated elements but make sure aria-describedby links the chip to the pin text.

June Park: accessibility concerns: keyboard users need a direct way to traverse pins. proposal: add a small focusable hit area (4x4?) next to the chip with aria-label="Open annotations for version vX". also support a screenreader-only list view of annotations for the current timeline viewport.

Rishi - PM: copy and product notes: default pin title format: "Annotation: <short note>". we should allow emojis and short markdown in the note. Also permission: who can create pins? orgs may want pins restricted to owners or to enable collaborative pins. track events: annotation_created, annotation_opened, annotation_edited, annotation_deleted.

Ana Varela: visual: pin icon should be subtle (outline thumbtack) and color-coded by tag (eg: incident, note, review). ensure color choices are colorblind-friendly (use patterns or icons + labels). hover reveals small preview tooltip. on mobile, tapping the chip should open a bottom-sheet with full annotations list.

a11y-bot: checklist: annotations must be reachable via keyboard, have descriptive aria-labels, provide aria-describedby on chips, ensure contrast >=4.5:1 for small text in tooltips, and provide an accessible list fallback. Announcements: when annotation added to current view, send polite aria-live update: "Annotation added to version vX".

Tom - Eng: keyboard order question: if annotations are focusable, we need to avoid adding too many tab stops when many versions have pins. suggestion: provide a global shortcut ("a") to toggle annotation navigation mode that restricts tabbing to pinned items only. in that mode left/right moves between pins and Enter opens detail. we can expose this in help.

June Park: good idea. for screen reader users we can also expose a landmark: `<section aria-label="Timeline annotations">` that contains a list of current pins. that list should be reachable from the main nav. keep descriptions short for SR consumption.

Rishi - PM: product tradeoff: first MVP: show pins on hover/expand, allow create/edit/delete for owners, and provide mobile bottom-sheet. advanced: shared pinboards and annotations search. instrument: annotation_navigation_mode_toggled, annotation_shortcut_used. target snapshot for release notes: "Add timeline annotations (beta)".

Ana Varela: micro-interaction: pin creation inline: click pin icon -> small popover with textarea (max 240 chars), tags dropdown, Save/Delete. Respect reduced-motion. For mobile bottom-sheet make sure keyboard doesn't push input behind virtual keyboard (use safe-area + scrollIntoView).

Tom - Eng: tech: we'll namespace CSS `.rw-annotation-pin` and add `data-annotation-id`. server: store pins keyed by model+version+org. render server-side hints to avoid load flicker. progressive enhancement: if JS off, show a link to annotation list page.

a11y-bot: extra: ensure edit/delete operations announce success/failure. when deleting, use an inline confirm (non-blocking). limit SR announcements to <200 chars. test with VoiceOver and NVDA.

June Park: action items: 1) Ana to add pin icon variants (default/incident/review) + mobile bottom-sheet mock. 2) Tom to prototype tabindex plan and annotation-navigation-mode toggling. 3) Rishi to draft permission model + telemetry events. 4) a11y-bot will add checklist to ticket. ETA: next sprint.

Rishi - PM: tagging @ana @tom @june - please post updated frames in the ticket and add PRD note about permission gating. :memo:

Ana Varela: will upload Figma frames tonight and include compact and expanded flows. thanks! :thumbsup:
